html:
The British province that ruled most of southern India from the city of Madras, now Chennai. It grew from a trading post into one of the three great presidencies of British India.

In 1639 the East India Company bought a strip of coast and built Fort St. George. Madras became the Company's base on the east coast. In the 1740s to 1760s it fought the French for control of the Carnatic, and won. The province then grew in steps: the Northern Circars in 1766, Malabar and Kanara after the defeat of Tipu Sultan of Mysore in 1799, and the Carnatic itself in 1801. It also ran Ceylon briefly in the 1790s.

Most land tax was collected directly from farmers, under the ryotwari system. Railways and irrigation came in the 1800s, but so did famine: the Great Famine of 1876 to 1878 killed millions. Many Tamil and Telugu workers left to labour abroad, as on the tea estates of Ceylon and in Malaya.

Under the British Raj Madras had elected ministers from the 1920s. After independence it became Madras State in 1950. In the 1950s it was split along language lines into Andhra, Kerala, Mysore and a Tamil remainder, renamed Tamil Nadu in 1969.
sum: The British province that ruled most of southern India from the city of Madras, now Chennai. It grew from a trading post into one of the three great presidencies of British India.
